releases.displayName: EA SPORTS FC™ 27 | Closed Beta Feedback Update

items.text: [p align="start"]During the EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Closed Beta, we heard your feedback across the game through the EA Closed Beta Forums, the FC 27 Closed Beta Player Feedback Portal, and Discord. We’ve been reviewing that feedback to better understand your experience and the topics that mattered most to you.

[p align="start"]In this Pitch Notes, we’ll cover improvements driven by your feedback across areas including physical play, Team Press, Lengthy players, and more. We’ll also provide more context on some of the topics you’ve raised and share our approach to gameplay updates during the launch period.

[p align="start"]We’ve been closely following player conversations and know there’s feedback about significant gameplay balance changes being made after launch. For EA SPORTS FC™ 27, we want to take a measured approach and do not plan on making significant gameplay balance changes in our early Title Updates.

[p align="start"]How the game is played and understood can evolve quickly during the opening weeks as players learn new mechanics, discover different ways to play, and build squads. Because of that, we don’t want to react quickly to early trends with significant balance changes. Instead, we’ll give the gameplay experience time to settle so we can better understand how the game develops and whether adjustments are needed.

[p align="start"]Our intention is to preserve the gameplay experience we’ve built for launch and give players time to learn and adapt to it. We’ll continue listening closely to your feedback throughout that period, which you can share through the FC Feedback Hub.

[p align="start"]We’ll still look to address bugs, unintended behaviours, and other issues that are significantly impacting the gameplay experience. In some cases, addressing these issues may have an impact on the balance of related gameplay systems. For example, addressing an unintended Goalkeeper behaviour could affect the balance between shooting and Goalkeeping more broadly. When fixes like these are needed, we’ll aim to make them as targeted as possible to address the specific issue while limiting their impact on the wider gameplay experience.

[p align="start"]Physical play and the Bruiser PlayStyle have been big topics coming out of the EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Closed Beta. We still want physical play to be a viable way to win the ball while defending, but we’ve made some changes to make Shoulder Challenges more consistent and address some unintended ways they could’ve been used.
[p align="start"]Shoulder Challenges should be most effective when the defender gets side-by-side with the ball carrier rather than attempting a challenge from behind.

[p align="start"]One behaviour we wanted to address was repeatedly pressing Shoulder Challenge while chasing an opponent until a challenge eventually triggered. Now, repeatedly pressing Shoulder Challenge in quick succession will cause the defender to stick out an arm and lose speed, making it more difficult to chase down an opponent by repeatedly using the input.

[p align="start"]When you get into the right position and time the challenge properly, physical defending remains effective. Strength continues to play an important role, with the Bruiser PlayStyle providing an additional benefit. We’ve also slightly reduced the additional benefit provided by Bruiser+.
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]Team Press is intended to be a way to apply pressure higher up the pitch, but we found it was also too effective when used close to your own goal. In those situations, AI teammates could automatically close down opponents and take too much of the defensive responsibility away from the user.

[p align="start"]To address this, Team Press will now have no effect while the ball is in your defensive third. This directly addresses one of the most common ways Team Press could be used to automatically pressure attackers close to goal, requiring the defending player to take more responsibility for applying pressure in these situations.

[p align="start"]When Team Press is used further up the pitch, defenders can still step towards their marked players, but will be less effective at applying pressure than midfielders and forwards. This also comes with a trade-off: as defenders move closer to their marked players, they can become more susceptible to passes played in behind the defensive line.

[p align="start"]We also heard feedback that defensive lines could sit higher than expected, even when using a lower Defensive Depth. We’ve made adjustments so that lower depth settings are more clearly reflected in how your defensive line positions itself, with defenders retreating sooner and maintaining a more conservative position to leave less space in behind. Your defensive line will still adjust to what’s happening on the pitch, so setting a low depth doesn’t mean your defenders will stay deep in every situation.

[p align="start"]Based on your feedback during the Closed Beta, we’ve looked at AcceleRATE itself as well as some of the other mechanics that were contributing to Lengthy players being particularly effective.

[p align="start"]As previously announced in the FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive, Triggered Runs will now have a limited distance. You’ll need to trigger another run if you want the player to continue their movement. This requires more active input when managing longer runs and also reduces some of the benefits Lengthy players could gain over extended distances.
[p align="start"]We’ve also made a couple of other changes to further address the effectiveness of Lengthy players.

[p align="start"]We’ve slightly reduced the impact of AcceleRATE profiles on a player’s running performance, bringing Explosive, Controlled, and Lengthy players a little closer together. This places greater emphasis on a player’s Acceleration and Sprint Speed Attributes.

[p align="start"]We’ve also adjusted the height threshold for female players to be eligible for the Lengthy AcceleRATE profile. In FC 27, female players will need to be at least 5’8” (172 cm) to be eligible for Lengthy.

[p align="start"]Together, we believe these changes provide a better balance between the different AcceleRATE profiles, while allowing each to remain useful depending on your players and your preferred style of play.

[p align="start"]We heard your feedback that Player Lock could be particularly effective with very little downside for an advanced mechanic. Based on that feedback, we’ve made some changes to introduce more of a risk-reward balance when using Player Lock.

[p align="start"]When you Player Lock away from the ball carrier, the ball carrier will no longer automatically dribble around or avoid defenders. Instead, they’ll continue moving in the direction they were already travelling.

[p align="start"]This gives the defending player a clearer opportunity to recognise the situation and apply pressure to the ball carrier, while requiring the attacking player to be more aware of what’s happening on the ball while controlling another player.
[p align="start"]We’ve also slightly increased the error in passes made by the CPU-controlled ball carrier during Player Lock, further adding to the risk-reward balance of using the feature.
[p align="start"]We want Player Lock to continue providing opportunities to create manual movement off the ball, while placing more responsibility on the player using it.
[p align="start"]As previously announced in the Gameplay Deep Dive, Dinked Passes are fully manual in EA SPORTS FC™ 27.

[p align="start"]Previously, Ground Pass and Through Pass could trigger different versions of the Dinked Pass, one toward a teammate and one into space. With Dinked Passes now being manual, where the ball goes will instead be determined by where you aim.

[p align="start"]During the Closed Beta, we also saw that Dinked Passes could be triggered accidentally when pressing Ground Pass multiple times. To address this, Dinked Passes can no longer be performed using the Ground Pass input. Double-tapping or repeatedly pressing Ground Pass will result in a regular Ground Pass.
[p align="start"]To perform a Dinked Pass, double tap Through Pass and manually aim where you want the ball to go.
[p align="start"]We’ve seen questions from the community about how the new Attacking Spatial Awareness system works alongside Player Roles.

[p align="start"]Player Roles continue to determine the types of runs a player can make based on their position and Role. For example, an Inside Forward can look to make runs into the space between the centre back and fullback, while a Winger will consider runs that better reflect their wider positioning.

[p align="start"]Role Familiarity then influences the urgency with which a player makes those available runs. Players with greater familiarity in a Role, including Role+ and Role++, will show more urgency when making those movements.
[p align="start"]Attacking Spatial Awareness doesn’t replace Player Roles. Instead, the two systems work together to influence a player’s attacking movement.

notes.title: Corner Kicks: What’s New in FC 27?

items.text: [p align="start"]We’ve seen questions around what is actually different about Corner Kicks in FC 27 since you could already control a player in the box in FC 26.

[p align="start"]While FC 26 gave you the ability to manually control a player in the box, the main difference with corners in FC 27 is the amount of assistance you get when manually positioning your player.

[p align="start"]EA SPORTS FC™ 27 gives you free movement and no longer moves your player toward the expected landing position of the ball. It’s now down to you to read the trajectory, get into the right position and time the run.

[p align="start"]The player you’re controlling matters too, as height and jumping ability can change where and when you want to attack the ball. A taller player with strong jumping, for example, may be able to meet the ball earlier in its trajectory. A player’s physical momentum also matters, so it’s not only about getting to the right spot, it’s also about how and when you arrive there.

[p align="start"]You can also use Shielding to help hold a good position once you’ve found it, or use the new Avoidance mechanic to slip past opponents and try to beat them to the best spot to attack the ball.

[p align="start"]Based on the feedback from the FC 27 Closed Beta, we’re making several refinements to CPU AI in Authentic Gameplay. In line with our approach to early gameplay updates, these changes are focused on targeted adjustments rather than significantly changing the overall balance of the gameplay experience.
[p align="start"]These adjustments include, but are not limited to, the following areas:
Difficulty Calibration: Tuning difficulty progression to create clearer differences between Professional, World Class, and Legendary difficulties.
Tactical Adjustments: The thresholds for certain CPU Sliders, such as Sliding Tackle Frequency, are being recalibrated for more dynamic and realistic tactical behavior.

AI Behavior: We are implementing several changes to improve how the CPU AI builds attacks, approaches 1v1 finishing opportunities, and defends against specific offensive maneuvers such as through passes and triggered runs in certain situations.
[p align="start"]We appreciate the detailed feedback you shared throughout the Closed Beta and will continue refining Authentic Gameplay ahead of launch.

items.text: Hey Steam Community!

We've updated match outcomes in FC 26 so that you can get a win sooner if the opponent Quits/Disconnects On A Draw during Live Events, Rivals, and Champions matches. One of these conditions must apply in order for a win to be awarded:
\ 10 minutes (in-game time) has passed. This was previously 20 minutes.
The quitting/disconnecting player concedes a penalty kick.
The quitting/disconnecting player has received a red card
A player can only receive a win from this 3 times a day, with the limit resetting at 00:00 UTC daily.

items.text: [p align="start"]We’re celebrating the summer of international football with The World’s Game Update for EA SPORTS FC™ 26, launching 28 May.

[p align="start"]Alongside PlayStyles changes and more gameplay updates based on your feedback, you'll be able to lead your nation to glory in a new 48-team international tournament mode starting 4 June, with 53 fully licensed and playable national teams, including 41 competing over the summer.

[p align="start"]The World’s Game Update also brings international action to Football Ultimate Team™ with a dedicated Event Hub, Festival of Football themed campaigns and more. Plus, log in and play FC 26 between 5 June and 24 July to earn a 93 OVR Festival of Football ICON Pelé and three ‘Choose Your Journey’ Evolutions.

[p align="start"]The World’s Game Update delivers a brand-new tournament mode launching 4 June, bringing the summer’s international action to EA SPORTS FC™ 26. With 53 fully licensed and playable national teams - including 41 that will be in action over the summer - you can choose from global powerhouses like Brazil, England, and France or emerging international stories like Cabo Verde, Uzbekistan, and more. Lead your nation to glory, rewrite history to create new international storylines, and experience new true-to-life stadiums including Gillette Stadium and BMO Field, alongside Central Maw - a new stadium built to capture the atmosphere of top-tier international football.

Celebrate his international achievements in 1970 with Evolutions inspired by key matches and tournament stages.

notes.title: Evo Undo, Festival of Football PlayStyles Lab & Evo Repeats

items.text: [p align="start"]As part of a server release following the World’s Game Update on 4 June, you’ll be able to roll back and fully reset Evolutions in your Club. If you reset an originally Tradable Player, they’ll return to their Tradable status.
[p align="start"][img src="https://drop-assets.ea.com/images/54AO7EfwTgiXY5DrC3pma8/58eee9f5aedb2ba161c445d79d51752e/Remove_All_Evo.png.png?im=AspectCrop=%2816,9%29,xPosition=0.25,yPosition=0.25"]
[p align="start"][img src="https://drop-assets.ea.com/images/2CDQPkpDljO0Et9wMKPr3C/28031a5d483a6af5d3190a3e11fa11d8/Remove_Last_Evo.png?im=AspectCrop=%2816,9%29,xPosition=0.25,yPosition=0.25"]

[p align="start"]We want your Evo choices to be meaningful to you. Previous Evo updates reduced the pressure of selecting the right player for each Evo, and we believe the Evo Undo change reduces the need to select the right evo for each of your players.

[p align="start"]We’ve heard your feedback that choosing your own PlayStyles matters. As we reflect on FUT™ Birthday Bakery Evolutions, this was a missing ingredient to allow you to experiment with new players and then sell them on the Transfer Market if you didn’t see them staying in your Club long term.
[p align="start"]In Festival of Football we’re introducing a new PlayStyles Lab, allowing you to choose your preferred PlayStyles and PlayStyles+ for the following:
Festival of Football: Star Performer
Festival of Football: National Pride
Festival of Football: National Pride Champions
Glory Hunters
[p align="start"]FUT Birthday items will also be eligible for the PlayStyles Lab, replacing the Birthday Bakery Evolutions.

[p align="start"]In addition, we’ll be introducing a new item type - Evo Repeatables, which will allow you to earn additional Evolution entries. You’ll see these rewards in upcoming Festival of Football content.

[p align="start"]Tokens are a brand new reward type that have been designed to give you greater choice over how you play and what you earn in FUT. Starting on 4 June you’ll be able to earn Festival of Football tokens across a range of game modes including;
Rivals
Squad Battles
Rush
Live Events
Select Objectives
Select SBCs
[p align="start"]We’re excited about the impact Tokens will have on FUT & your rewards. Starting in Festival of Football, Tokens will become the primary way to earn rewards in FUT each week.

[p align="start"]No matter how or where you play FUT, from Season 8 onwards the aim is that you will feel better rewarded for the time you spend playing in game. By unifying mode rewards into Tokens you’ll be able to progress towards the same rewards no matter your mode, giving you greater choice in where you play.
[p align="start"]Like you see currently in FUT, higher rank finishes will reward you with both Tokens & Additional Rewards for competing at the highest level.
[p align="start"]As we balance FUT for the entire community, we’re introducing a cap on how many Tokens you can earn each week, placing greater emphasis on the rewards you choose to pursue.

[p align="start"]Throughout Festival of Football, you’ll be able to earn up to 1,000 Tokens each week (5,000 Tokens in total). Tokens offer a more flexible and reliable way to earn rewards across modes.

[p align="start"]We expect that skilled players may be able to earn 1,000 Tokens through playing Squad Battles, Rivals or Live Events and completing special Objectives and SBCs each week. We’ll review this and listen to feedback to understand if this is an area we want to make changes to in the future.

[p align="start"]Festival of Football Tokens are earned only through playing FUT and will not be made available inside Store Pack offers.

[p align="start"]Tokens will have a dedicated Store with Players, Packs, Evolutions, and Club Customisation content. To ensure that your choices are more meaningful to you, you will not be able to unlock everything in the store.
To cater for a variety of players across the Season, the Store will have a range of prices
Rewards up to 300 tokens can be redeemed instantly or weekly
Rewards up to 1,000 tokens will require multiple play sessions to unlock
Rewards up to 2,500 tokens will need to be worked toward over the course of the Season
An important call out is that the highest reward available in the store will be roughly half of the total limit
Weekly Refreshes
Each week we’ll swap out Weekly Refreshes for lower cost rewards to add variety and better connect to new campaigns that release each week
Season long planning
Bigger rewards will be persistent throughout Festival of Football to allow you to plan towards any rewards you want to earn over a longer time period

[p align="start"]In Season 8, we’ll also be introducing FUT Champions Tokens and a FUT Champions Store featuring a range of rewards, including a rotating selection of special Red FUT Champions Player Items each week. Champions Tokens give you greater choice over your Champions rewards no matter your skill level.
[p align="start"]For those who pick up a handful of wins each weekend, you can get weekly rewards or save Tokens over multiple weekends in a Season for bigger rewards.

[p align="start"]For those who pick up multiple wins each weekend, we think this change will give you greater choice over the rewards you get. Higher win finishes will still provide additional Coins on top of Champions Tokens, to reward you for pushing for your best finish each weekend.
[p align="start"]We believe Tokens will give you greater control over the weekends you choose to play in.

[p align="start"]As mentioned, this is the first time we’ll be introducing Tokens, and we’ll be taking your feedback on board. As with all of our newest features we are excited to see how this one evolves in the future.

notes.title: Festival of Football: Journey of Nations

items.text: [p align="start"]Journey of Nations introduces an Event Hub for the Festival of Football Season in Football Ultimate Team™. Each week you’ll need to assemble international themed squads, travelling across five continents and completing over 250 challenges to earn epic rewards for your Club. Each region's Objectives & rewards will be themed around iconic players, historic nations, and emerging stars.
[p align="start"]See the Festival of Football schedule below:
North America - Thursday, 4 June 2026
Asia + Oceania - Friday, 12 June 2026
Africa - Friday, 19 June 2026
South America - Friday, 26 June 2026
Europe - Friday, 3 July 2026

[p align="start"]Throughout Festival of Football we want you to build your international Ultimate Team. To help fans across the world build their dream squad we’ll be adding over 100 new international players to the FUT pool of items this summer.
[p align="start"]We're also excited to introduce 2 brand new ICONS; Rivellino & Mario Kempes.
[p align="start"]They’ll debut with special Greats of the Game Versions on 19 June, before their Base versions are available in the FUT pool of items for Packs from 26 June.
[p align="start"]The following five campaigns will also be released into the Football Ultimate Team™ pool of items between 5 June and 24 July.
Path To Glory: 5 June – 19 June
[p align="start"]Path to Glory opens the Festival of Football celebrations, following the journey of each nation with live Player Items that upgrade alongside the international action.
Greats of the Game: 19 June – 26 June
[p align="start"]Greats of the Game is all about the legends, introducing two new ICONS, Mario Kempes and Rivellino, to honour big name players who defined eras of The World’s Game.
Glory Hunters: 26 June – 10 July
[p align="start"]Glory Hunters brings PlayStyle customisation to selected Player Items for more control over squad building.
Phenoms: 10 July – 17 July
[p align="start"]Phenoms shines a light on football’s next generation. Spotlighting young players and debutants looking to stand out as the world watches on.
Summer Stars: 17 July – 24 July
[p align="start"]The Festival of Football finale culminates in a celebration of the biggest moments and greatest performers.
[p align="start"]We’ll also release a range of recurring Programs including Showdowns, Star Performers and National Pride.
[p align="start"]As we continue to monitor and respond to community feedback, we’re making the following PlayStyles changes to improve gameplay balance.
Bruiser

[p align="start"]Following feedback surrounding shoulder challenge outcomes feeling too impactful, especially when using the Bruiser PlayStyle, we have updated both Bruiser and Bruiser+ to better balance between PlayStyles and Attributes.
[p align="start"]Attributes and PlayStyles Balance
Slightly reduced the boost to shoulder challenges from Bruiser and Bruiser+
Added a slight boost to the receiver of the shoulder challenge if they have Enforcer or Enforcer+
This boost matches the one made to Bruiser/Bruiser+
[p align="start"]Improved Shoulder Challenge Outcomes
Improved shoulder challenge outcomes so stumble direction and force now better reflect the difference in Strength and PlayStyles between players.
Note that players with a clear Strength and PlayStyle advantage while defending are able to push the dribbler off the ball like before
If the advantage lies more with the dribbler they are not pushed away as easily and have a chance to recover the ball
This effect scales with the difference in Strength and PS boost between the players resulting in more authentic outcomes overall
[p align="start"]Improved Detection of Challenges from Behind
Added logic to predict when a shoulder challenge may hit the back of the opponent, and cancel the challenge if so
[p align="start"]Other Changes
Addressed a visual bug where the Bruiser+ icon displays when the PlayStyle wasn’t in effect
Intercept
[p align="start"]We’ve also made the following change to the Intercept PlayStyle to make Attributes more impactful while preserving the PlayStyle benefit:
Added the ability for players without the Intercept PlayStyle but with a 90+ Interceptions attribute rating to have access to the same animations as those with the PlayStyle.

[p align="start"]We had a lot of feedback from the community regarding the Team Press tactic being overused. We’ve made the following changes to AI-controlled defenders to encourage more tactical options:
Reduced pressure on the ball carrier when Team Press is activated in the defensive half
If the user controls a defender in position to mark the ball carrier, AI defenders will not double up on the ball carrier
If the user controls a defender further away from the ball defender, an AI controlled defender will try to contain the ball carrier but not aggressively pressure them
Reduced marking tightness of all AI opponents when Team Press is activated in the defensive half
Marking becomes looser as the opponent advances closer to goal
When Team Press is activated in the attacking half, these changes do not apply. AI defenders will behave as before, aggressively pressuring the ball carrier and contextually doubling up

[p align="start"]The International Men’s Tournament will also be available in Career, following the same structure and rules as The World’s Game mode. Alongside this, additional national teams have been fully licensed and added, and you can add a national team to manage at the beginning of any new save.
[p align="start"]The following new content is also coming to Career:
Added End of Season Live Starting Points, allowing you to jump into a save just before The International Men’s Tournament begins
Following a server release after The World’s Game Update, players will also be able to select a national team at the start of a new Live Starting Point
Added Festival of Football themed ICONs and Heroes
Weekly releases of Festival of Football themed Manager Live Challenges starting 5 June
New Season objectives for playing with national teams
Complete X amount of Y Category Name Challenges

Improved accuracy and speed of ground passing, with impact being most noticeable on players with higher passing attributes.
Added the ability for players without the Incisive Pass PlayStyle but with high attributes in Short Pass, Long Pass, and Curve to contextually curve through balls.

Ground passes performed with Tiki Taka PlayStyle still benefit from the overall improvements in accuracy and speed listed above, ensuring the PlayStyle remains a useful attacking option.
The accuracy of lofted ground and through passes using the Inventive PlayStyle and Inventive PlayStyle+ has been slightly increased.

This is to slightly compensate for the accuracy reduction to lofted passes mentioned in the passing section. With the PlayStyle+, lofted passes will still be slightly less accurate than before the patch

items.text: Throughout February, we’ve continued tracking your feedback across all modes. Today we wanted to highlight upcoming changes to PlayStyles and address the recent fix to Finesse Shots.

We recently addressed the Finesse Shot issue. The problem was resolved by rolling back a change from Title Update 1.4.2. In those patch notes, the change was described as: "Inaccurate knuckle ball shots could have occurred more often than intended."
Following the rollback, Finesse Shots should now be performing as expected. We’ll continue monitoring feedback and gameplay data, but this fix is now live.

A major theme in your feedback has been that attributes should feel more powerful and impactful, with PlayStyles enhancing players rather than defining their entire effectiveness. In an upcoming update, we’ll be tuning attributes and several PlayStyles to better reflect that philosophy.

items.text: Tiki Taka, Incisive Pass, Inventive Pass. We will also be bringing some overall changes to Power Shots and Chip Shots.

notes.title: Goalkeeper Movement Will Be Less Effective

items.text: [p align="start"]We’ve been looking at Goalkeeper Movement for a while now, finding more ways to make it more balanced.

[p align="start"]We’ve heard varied opinions about this mechanic from your feedback across all of our sources. One thing that’s clear is that there’s an opportunity to find more of a balance between shooting and goalkeeping.
[p align="start"]With that in mind, we’ll be adjusting Goalkeeper Movement to be less effective in a December update. We’ll share full details on this change closer to the update.

notes.title: How We’re Using Your Recent Feedback

items.text: [p align="start"]We’ve seen community discussions that we’re making design decisions based on the feedback of those with the most powerful voices online. We consider many feedback sources for every game issue or update, including the Player Feedback Portal, social media, Design Councils, EA Forums, Steam Community Hub, the FC Pro Discord, the Global Discord, and more.

[p align="start"]When we use platforms such as Discord polls to get feedback about certain features, we’re getting a quick pulse check of your general opinions. The polls themselves are one aspect of the overall feedback we review before committing to any updates.
[p align="start"]To learn more about the feedback process and the best ways to let us know your thoughts, check out our Feedback Deep Dive.

notes.title: [p align="start"]The below change was made in FC 26 v1.2.0

items.text: Slightly reduced how tightly AI defenders will mark pass receivers on the edge of their box.

[p align="start"]We made this change after the improvements to jockeying because we saw from your feedback that you felt that user controlled players could sometimes sit back on defense and let AI teammates do the hard work in some scenarios.

[p align="start"]This is an area of the game you give us a lot of feedback on, and similar to Goalkeeper Movement, it’s the type of feedback that can vary significantly between different types of players.

[p align="start"]We’re continuing to watch this space closely, if we make further tweaks they’ll likely be incremental so that we don’t completely shift the balance of the game with a single update. We’ll let you know of any changes in this space ahead of making any updates.

[p align="start"]In the past few weeks a change was made to Controlled Sprint Dribbling that slowed it down, the magnitude of this change was unintended, and we quickly reverted it once we saw how it affected the game across the wider player base
[p align="start"]We’re committed to ensuring movement in FC 26 feels as responsive as it can. Thank you for your feedback that enabled us to do a quick Live Tuning Update.

notes.title: [p align="start"]In FC 26 v1.1.3 we updated the CPU AI* to

items.text: Look for passes more often and make quicker decisions about them.
Dribble more effectively with sharper turns, less straightforward movement, and less dwelling on the ball.
Switch players on defense more often in situations where trailing the runner is not beneficial.
[p align="start"]*The term CPU AI here is referring to the virtual user controlling the team you're playing against in offline matches. This update did not affect the player versus player experience.
[p align="start"]The full breakdown of the changes can be found in the following social thread and we’ll continue to monitor your feedback on this topic.

[p align="start"]We’ve seen your feedback that the CPU AI in Squad Battles can hold the ball for too long and plays an overly possession based game at times. We’re planning to make the Squad Battles CPU AI further focus on moving the ball forward and creating chances quicker.

[p align="start"]The intent here is to create a more fun gameplay experience in the defensive phase, reducing frustrating off the ball moments where you previously had to chase CPU AI defenders and midfielders passing the ball around without much attacking progress.
[p align="start"]We want to make sure we take the time to get this balance right and will be targeting an early 2026 update.

[p align="start"]We’re in the process of carefully reviewing your responses,looking for commonalities and trends behind the issues reported that can help our ongoing internal investigations.
[p align="start"]While we don’t have a more direct update to share at this time, we’ll continue to share information around PC improvements as they happen.

[p align="start"]Recently we investigated your reports of Multi-Swap in Football Ultimate Team causing potential stability issues, and we released FC 26 v1.2.1 which addressed some stability issues that could have occurred, including the Multi-Swap one.
[p align="start"]We recently released a small stability update, and we’re planning a larger update in early December.
[p align="start"]Our next title update will address certain issues, introduce new additions, and bring some holiday cheer to FC 26. We’ll share more details in the next few weeks.

notes.title: Faster Jockeying For More Effective Manual Defending

items.text: As we mentioned in our October Feedback Update, FC 26 v1.1.0 aims to empower manual defending. Here’s the change we’re making:
Slightly increased Sprint Jockey speed for user controlled players.
Moderately increased Jockey and Sprint Jockey responsiveness for user controlled players.
With this change we’re looking to have more of a balance between attacking and defending, but without compromising the attacking responsiveness you enjoy.
We’ve heard your feedback about skilled dribblers being too strong when attacking, and we want you to have an improved defensive option when dealing with them.
Here’s a quick comparison of a defender Jockeying before and after FC 26 1.1.0:
Jockey_B&A_Final_2.mp4

As usual, we’ll continue to closely watch your feedback in this space. You can expect to see a poll about this change in our Discord soon, and you can give us more detailed feedback in the FC Feedback Portal.

notes.title: More Aggressive Marking During Competitive Gameplay Kick-Offs

items.text: FC 26 v1.1.0 introduces an additional change to kick-off defending aimed at making kick-offs significantly harder to score from.
\[Competitive Gameplay] Increased aggressiveness of player marking that only applies to the defensive side’s AI players around kick-off.
We heard your feedback that kick-offs previously led to too many goals being scored, and now you can expect to see the defensive side’s AI players work harder and more urgently to prevent that.
Keep in mind that this change only applies to kick-offs, AI player marking has not changed for other scenarios, and this update does not affect Authentic Gameplay at all.

notes.title: Additional Gameplay Improvements Based On Your Feedback

items.text: While the main gameplay focus of FC 26 v1.1.0 is to empower manual defending and reduce kick-off goals, we’re adding in a number of improvements based on your feedback. For example, we’re:
Making Through Passes more consistent, less assisted, and respectful of your aim input.
Lowering Controlled Sprint Dribbling speed.
Improving goalkeeper in specific cases, such as during corner kicks.
Plus we’re addressing a number of issues you’ve told us about.
To see the full list of gameplay updates in FC 26 v1.1.0, be sure to check out our update notes on the EASFC Tracker.

notes.title: New Objective Tracking In Football Ultimate Team

items.text: We’re delighted to be able to bring you a much-requested Football Ultimate Team feature, Objective Tracking.

Following a Server Release shortly after FC 26 v1.1.0, you’ll be able to favorite Objectives and Objective Groups in Football Ultimate Team. Favorited Objectives and Objective Groups will show up in the pause menu when you’re playing, including Evolutions and Rivals Bounties, and you can track your progress as it happens.
Your favorited Objectives and Objective Groups will also have their own dedicated UI tab in the FUT menus.
You can also get gameplay notifications for completed Objectives, which can be controlled through Game Settings.

notes.title: New Evolution Consumable Preview In Football Ultimate Team

items.text: Following a Server Release shortly after FC 26 v1.1.0, you’ll be able to see Evolution challenge requirements and player eligibility criteria before even owning the corresponding EVO.

notes.title: Here’s how you can access these previews

items.text: 1. View an Evo consumable.
2. Follow the on-screen button prompt for previewing (it’s the same as previewing Player Items).
3. Enter a filtered version of the Evo hub showing your specific Evo being previewed.
4. View entry requirements, challenges, and rewards/upgrades.
5. You can browse through your Club for eligible Items and preview how they would look like in the Evo if you were to obtain it.
We know that you have to make a lot of choices as you build and upgrade your Squad in Football Ultimate Team, and we want to make the process easier and more informed in the Evolution space.

With the new preview functionality, you can see key details before using an Evolution Consumable reward, whether it comes from Squad Building Challenges, Objectives, or other rewards sources. This gives us more flexibility to include a wider range of Evolution Consumable rewards across the mode.

As the FC 26 Ultimate Team experience continues to evolve, we’ve been listening closely to your feedback. Heading into Season 2, we’re introducing a series of updates aimed at making your experience more rewarding, balanced, and engaging across the mode.

From balance adjustments to updates in Live Events and Rivals, to Evolutions design changes, our goal remains the same, to ensure FC 26 delivers a fun and fulfilling experience for every type of player.
Let’s dive into what’s changing and why.
Division Rivals Rewards
We’ve heard that weekly rewards in Division Rivals haven’t felt as reflective of your effort and engagement as they should.

To address this, Season 2 will introduce increased Rivals rewards, with a particular emphasis on tradeable content and FUT Coin rewards. These changes are designed to make participation in Rivals feel more meaningful and rewarding each week.
In FC 26 we shifted the focus of EVOs to provide smaller, repeatable Attribute boosts with open requirements in order to provide maximum flexibility.
However, we heard your feedback that we focused too much on these types of boosts at the start of Season 1 and that it was taking too long to upgrade your favourite lower-rated items.

In the past couple of weeks, we’ve made changes to focus more on EVOs that provide bigger, more comprehensive upgrades, with differing maximum OVR requirements. This allows us to tailor upgrades that are meaningful for Player Items across various OVRs.
This focus will continue throughout Ultimate Scream to help you upgrade more of your favourite players through EVOs.
Live Events, Tournaments, and Gauntlet have created some of the most exciting moments in FC 26, giving you new ways to compete, experiment with diverse squads, and earn exclusive rewards.

However, we’ve heard your feedback that many rewards have felt too difficult to achieve. We’re always evaluating the competitive balance across FUT, and we agree that some rewards have required more effort than intended.

In Season 2, we’ll be adjusting how value is delivered in these modes by placing greater emphasis on play-to-earn objectives rather than win-to-earn ones. This means you’ll start seeing objectives that reward both consistent play and skill.
For example, a Tournament objective group might let you earn rewards by winning 3 matches or playing 6 matches.

That said, we still want to celebrate players who rise to the top. In Season 2, expect a stronger focus on exclusive cosmetic rewards for those who demonstrate competitive excellence across in these limited time modes.
In FC 26, we introduced limited checkpoints to help support your progression in Rivals.
Overall, we’ve seen positive feedback in this space. However, we’ve also heard from some players that it can feel frustrating to get stuck in Divisions above your true skill level.

To address this, we’ll be removing the permanent checkpoint at the start of Division 6, allowing players to relegate into Division 7. This change is intended to make progression smoother and better aligned with each player’s current skill.
Career Mode Manager Market Improvements
We’re making improvements to the Manager Market logic for a more authentic and refined experience.
We’re addressing a number of issues that resulted in managers switching too early, or moving to teams that weren’t an intended fit for them.

We are also tuning the AI Manager job security logic to allow for a more refined behaviour, decreasing the incidence of unrealistic board expectations set for managers hired during the season leading to unintended manager movements.
Additionally, we’ve made improvements to the Manager Market mail notifications system, addressing issues where updates were triggered in unintended scenarios or too often.
We’re also addressing stability issues manifesting in both Manager and Player Career Modes and restoring the Trainer functionality’s availability in Manager Career Pause Menu.

And last but not least, we’re addressing a series of visual issues related to some Social Media posts’ composition, the number of roles presented in scout reports, and Deeper Simulation stats permanency across seasons for players transferring across leagues.
Clubs Archetype Max Level Increase

Alongside Season 2, we’ll be increasing the Clubs Archetype Max Level from 50 to 60. The Consumable max level remains the same. You can also expect to see one new customizable PlayStyle slot unlocked at level 60. You’ll now have a maximum of 300 Attribute Points you can use.
Look out for the next step up in Max Level in December!
PC Optimization

As our PC optimization efforts continue, we’ll be reaching out to players more directly to better understand the issues you’re facing, since our game runs on a wide variety of hardware. In FC 26 v1.1.0, we’re addressing the following PC specific issues:
Graphics settings could have reset when exiting Game Settings.
Improved shader caching to address some cases of performance drops when matches start.
Some textures could have appeared incorrectly on some Intel GPUs.
Addressed instances of vibrations and haptics being too low when using a PS5 controller.
This issue could have also occurred on PS5.
Simplified Aspect Ration setting list.

We released EA SPORTS FC 26 last month and a lot’s happened since then. On our side, we released 3 title updates driven by your feedback, addressed a number of emergent issues, and we’ve been closely following your feedback through the Feedback Portal, Discord, and social media.
In this article we’re covering your feedback over the past month, what we’ve done about it so far, and what we’re going to do in the future.
So let’s start with your biggest feedback topic so far, defending.

2. Kick-Offs Are Getting Harder To Score From In Competitive Gameplay

What You’ve Told Us

Defending against dribblers can feel too difficult, especially with their precise movements around the edge of the box, resulting in a potentially increased threat of goal-scoring chances and overly high scorelines.
What We’ve Done So Far

We’ve been following your feedback for weeks on this topic and wanted to make sure that we gave it time to evolve before considering any changes. FC 26 is a new game and it’s important to give you time to get familiar with its mechanics.
So for the time being, we made one update in this space in FC 26 version 1.0.4:
Addressed cases of players not being able to perform Physical Tackles, especially instances that occurred when the player had specific PlayStyles (eg. Bruiser).
What We’re Doing Next
We’re going to be making improvements to Jockeying responsiveness.
You might have seen us briefly mention this on our socials and the EASFC Tracker already, but we’re looking at empowering manual defending in an update that’s being planned for the end of October.
We want to give you an experience that has more of a balance between attacking and manual defending, but without compromising on the responsiveness of dribbling that you’ve told us you enjoy.
While we’re on the topic of defending, let’s take a look at another change we’ll be making.

notes.title: Kick-Offs Are Getting Harder To Score From In Competitive Gameplay

items.text: What You’ve Told Us
Defenders can give too much room to attackers during kick-offs, causing an increase in potential attacking threats resulting from a kick-off.
In practice, this has led to too many goals getting scored from kick-offs.
What We’ve Done So Far

notes.title: We started updating kick-offs in v1.0.3

items.text: The defending team will now position themselves more compactly for a short period of time after a kick off.
Updated positions of defending players prior to kick off for all formations.
However, we’ve seen from your feedback that there’s more room for improvement here, as we mentioned on social media previously.
What We’re Doing Next
We’re going to be making further improvements to AI defensive positioning during kick-offs.

With this update, we're planning on implementing more aggressive man marking that only applies to the defensive side around kick-off. This is in order to reduce the amount of goalscoring threats that can occur due to general kick-off positioning. Like with the Jockeying change, we’re targeting the end of October for this update.

By the way, as you might have seen from FC 26 v.1.0.4, these kick-off changes are intended for Competitive gameplay. We want to ensure that Authentic gameplay continues to provide a different experience that’s more true-to-football with an emphasis on immersion.
We Tackled A Number Of Emergent Issues And Feedback You Told Us About

Our teams are always looking to address emergent issues and give you the best in-game experience possible, and we want to say thank you for helping us recognize and investigate new issues as they happen.
Below are our updates on a number of emergent issues and feedback you’ve told us about.
Matchmaking In Football Ultimate Team Champions
We discovered that the first FUT Champions of the season had a matchmaking issue and we addressed it server-side as fast as we could.
What happened was that the Form aspect of FUT Champs matchmaking wasn’t quite working as intended, so there was more potential skill level variety in the opponents you faced.

While matchmaking is always complex and tries to give you the best available match at any given time, generally speaking we can say that you can expect to be playing with players who are in similar Form as you in FUT Champions matches.
Career Mode Contract And Transfer Negotiations

You’ve told us about several Manager Career issues that were impacting contract negotiations and transfers, with players seemingly communicating to managers in ways that are contradictory to their actual contracts and transfers.
We’ve been addressing instances of these situations occurring across FC 26 v.1.0.3 and v1.0.4, and we’re continuing to look at your feedback for future updates

Impacted players have been contacted in-game with correct rewards.
Addressed incorrect FUT Challengers Objectives progress.

We also continue to see your feedback around Evolutions and Transfer Market volatility. We’ll share updates with you around this feedback and what we’re doing next week when we can go into more detail for you.
PC Optimization And Dropped Controller Inputs
We’ve seen your feedback around technical performance on PC and controllers dropping inputs.

As we’ve shared in past updates, we’ve been addressing instances of these issues with just about every new version of the game. In FC 26 v1.0.3, we addressed an issue with your graphics settings being incorrectly saved, which may have impacted your overall experience at times. We continue to listen to your feedback in this space and are planning to address another batch of issues later this month.

To help mitigate some of the issues on PC, we want to share more details about how your experience can be impacted. Playing FC 26 offline and online is a bit of a different experience for your PC, which is why some players only experience issues in online matches.

If your PC is running the game offline close to its performance limits with no issues, but you run into online issues, this can happen because online play needs consistent performance in order for your game to stay in sync with others. The combination of online play with PC hardware that is pushing itself can result in issues occurring that you might not see otherwise.
We know that on PC you want to play the game as maxed out as possible, and we see the need to create in-game indicators for when your PC is struggling to achieve your desired settings.

We’ll continue to work on PC optimization with upcoming updates, and we’ll be looking to reach out to players more directly to better understand the issues you’re facing since the variety of hardware that runs our game is quite significant.

In the meantime, if you’re experiencing optimization or controller issues, lowering your graphics settings a little bit can eliminate some cases of that happening. Again, we know that’s not exactly what you want to hear at this time, but it is a workaround for a number of players, and we’ll keep working on improving optimization in general.
General Connectivity And General Matchmaking
While the period around FC 26 launch has been fairly smooth overall, we know that there have been several situations where players were affected by connectivity and matchmaking issues.

For example, there was an issue getting into the game as it launched that we addressed as fast as possible, and there was a day where many players were not able to matchmake properly. There’s even been a case of players in certain regions being affected by their ISPs preventing them from accessing the game.
We’ll continue to address these emergent issues as they pop up and provide updates on them as they happen on our X and WhatsApp channels.
We’re looking to release FC 26 v1.1 before the end of the month and include the changes we’ve mentioned throughout this article.
We’ll be sharing many more details on v1.1 next week as we finish making it, but here’s a quick preview of what you can expect around the time it releases:
A brand new Season, Season Pass, and more Evolutions.
Improvements to manual defending and kick-offs.
Ultimate Team Objective Tracking, Consumable Evolution Previews, and new SBC sorting filters.
Manager Market improvements, including addressing managers switching to teams that don’t seem like a great fit.
An increase to the Clubs Archetype max level.
Additional PC optimizations.
And much more.
